content.text:
I've gathered enough to understand the cause, but the fix is a platform-side decision with security implications, so I'll escalate rather than unilaterally recommend it.

Cause (from controller logs on `ingress-nginx-controller-5c8f9d7b6-qh4tn`):
```
annotation group ConfigurationSnippet contains risky annotation based on ingress configuration
skipping annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet on ingress legacy/legacy-portal:
Snippet directives are disabled by the Ingress administrator (allow-snippet-annotations=false)
```
The weekend upgrade moved ingress-nginx to v1.12.1, where `allow-snippet-annotations` defaults to `false` (hardening after CVE-2021-25742). The `legacy-portal` Ingress is unchanged and healthy (both pods Running/Ready), but its `configuration-snippet` (which carries the regex `rewrite ... redirect` the owner relies on) is now silently dropped, so `/old/...` falls through to the backend and returns 404.

Why I'm not just telling the owner to "fix it":
- The owner is in the `legacy` namespace and cannot change the ingress-nginx controller ConfigMap.
- Re-enabling `allow-snippet-annotations: "true"` globally reverses a deliberate security hardening and affects every tenant on the shared controller; it should also be paired with an `annotations-risk-level`/snippet allowlist decision.
- The documented Kubernetes guidance is only that controller-specific behavior must be checked against the controller's own docs [cite: concepts/services-networking/ingress-controllers#using-multiple-ingress-controllers-1], which doesn't by itself authorize the policy change.

input.reason: Root cause confirmed: ingress-nginx v1.12.1 (upgraded over the weekend) is dropping the legacy-portal Ingress's nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet because the controller is running with allow-snippet-annotations=false (see controller log: "skipping annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet on ingress legacy/legacy-portal: Snippet directives are disabled by the Ingress administrator"). The legacy-portal pods are healthy. The fix requires a platform-side policy decision on the shared ingress-nginx controller — either re-enable snippet annotations (and set an appropriate snippet allowlist / annotations-risk-level) in the controller ConfigMap, or migrate the legacy regex redirects to a supported mechanism. Both options are outside what the ticket owner can apply and have security/multi-tenant implications, so a human platform engineer should choose and implement.
